newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Senate race a dead heat, polls finds.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Senate race a dead heat, polls finds.

text.p: Mass. Sen. John Kerry and challenger to his seat Gov. William Weld each picked up the endorsement of a Boston newspaper Wednesday as two new polls showed the race remains a statistical dead heat.

The Democratic incumbent, who won the endorsement of the Boston Globe, has a 46 percent to 42 percent lead over Weld, within the survey's five percent margin of error, according to a poll by the Boston Herald and WCVB-TV.
Nine percent of the respondents were unsure and three percent sided with a third candidate.
The poll is the third in the past two weeks by the Boston Herald, which showed Kerry with a slight lead over the Republican Governor, who picked up the endorsement of the Boston Herald Wednesday.

The survey was conducted late Monday and Tuesday after Monday's feisty debate, the eighth and last face-off between the two. Yet the poll of 410 likely voters found that three-quarters did not even tune in to the debate and those who did rated it a tie.

"There was no huge boost either way," said Kelly Myers, director of the University of New Hampshire Survey Center, which conducted the poll. "Despite the candidates' best efforts to move the electorate through the TV ads and the ferocious debates, the voters aren't moving one way or another."
A Boston Globe poll showed Kerry leading by 44 percent to 38 percent, with 14 percent undecided. The survey of 400 voters taken Monday and Tuesday night has a five percent margin of error.

Weld, who has been blasted by his opponent as a foot soldier of Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, has issued television ads linking Kerry with former Mass. Gov. and Democratic presidential candidate Michael Dukakis.
The ads say that Kerry, who served as lieutenant governor to Dukakis from 1983 to 1984, is "still proud of the Dukakis-Kerry years when every year they raised taxes to pay for wasteful spending."
Dukakis lashed out at Weld in the Boston Herald, saying, "If Weld wants to run against me, engage in a debate with me about the state's fiscal condition, have him make some time after he gets beat."
